messages:
alice_support: Customer reports rerank returns scores assigned to the wrong query when a per-query candidate list is empty. They see items from later queries attached to earlier ones.
jamie_eng: Can you share the exact request/response and any trace ids?
alice_support: Minimal repro (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/rerank/batch
{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
  "candidates_per_query": [
    [{"id":"a"},{"id":"b"}],
    [],
    [{"id":"c"}]
  ]
}
```
Truncated response they saw:
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_index":0, "scores": [0.9, 0.1]},
    {"query_index":1, "scores": [0.7]},    // incorrect: input was empty
    {"query_index":2, "scores": [0.5]}
  ]
}
```
alice_support: So q2 had no candidates but got a score (looks like q3's candidate moved).
jamie_eng: Thanks. Any request_id / trace id from the backend?
alice_support: trace_id=trace-0a1b2c. Server log shows: `WARN candidate_index_shift: gap at query=1 offset=2`
jamie_eng: That log line is helpful. My hypothesis: when flattening per-query candidate arrays we drop empty buckets but still emit result offsets assuming they existed. That would shift subsequent offsets left.
sasha_prod: I ran a local e2e with the same payload and can reproduce. Steps: 1) curl the batch payload with the empty list in the middle 2) observe result length != sum of per-query candidate lengths 3) scores line up with wrong query indices.
maya_oncall: No infra alerts or OOMs. This looks purely transformation/serialization logic in the rerank service.
jamie_eng: I will add a unit test for mixing empty lists + singleton lists and patch the flattener to keep zero-length placeholders in the flattened index mapping. Assigning to myself, will push fix + integration test.
rerank-bot: created issue RERANK-457: preserve-empty-buckets; linked PR #1289
alice_support: Customer updated. Workaround: ensure callers include an explicit placeholder (e.g., `[null]` or `{}`) for empty per-query candidate lists until patch lands. Sent ETA ~48 hours. :thumbsup:
jamie_eng: quick note — also add validation to return 400 if the top-level arrays lengths mismatch to catch similar malformed requests.
